hero.title: Terms and Definitions
hero.description: This section presents the main concepts, indicators, and terms used by Delivery Worker Atlas. The definitions explain both concepts related to platform work and the way specific measures are produced and used by the project.

terms.definition: A finite sequence of computational instructions or rules used to process information and produce a result or decision. In delivery platforms, algorithms can help match orders with workers, calculate routes and estimated times, or determine which tasks are offered to whom.

The use of software-based procedures and data to organize, allocate, monitor, evaluate, or influence work. In delivery platforms, this may involve automated order assignment, performance ratings, incentives, and account restrictions. These systems can shape workers’ opportunities and autonomy, even when human supervisors are not directly involved.

The degree of control workers have over decisions about their work, including when and where to work, which tasks to accept, and how to perform them. In platform delivery, the freedom to log on or reject an order does not necessarily imply control over prices, access to tasks, performance evaluation, or platform rules.

A mobile application used to request, organize, assign, track, or complete deliveries. Some delivery apps function as digital labour platforms by coordinating paid work between customers, businesses, and couriers; others may only support logistics or recordkeeping. Their functions and degree of control over workers vary.

The length of the route covered by a worker during a defined period or activity, usually expressed in kilometres. It may include trips to pick up and deliver orders and, depending on the measurement method, travel between orders or while waiting for work. Analyses must specify which movements are counted and how distance is measured.

An agreement establishing the terms under which a person performs work for another party, including obligations, remuneration, and applicable rights. The legal status of delivery workers differs across countries and arrangements; signing a platform’s terms of service does not, by itself, settle whether an employment relationship exists.

The total amount recorded as earned from work before subtracting work-related expenses. Depending on the dataset, it may include payments for deliveries, bonuses, and tips. It should not be confused with the amount remaining after fuel, maintenance, vehicle rental, or other operating costs.

Gross earnings minus the work-related expenses included in the calculation, over the same reference period. Net earnings provide an estimate of the amount remaining after operating costs, but are not necessarily equivalent to take-home pay after taxes, social contributions, or every unrecorded expense.

The movement of people, goods, vehicles, and information through urban space. In delivery work, it includes couriers’ journeys between commercial establishments, customers, and waiting areas, shaped by infrastructure, demand, platform decisions, and unequal access to different parts of the city.

Costs incurred in carrying out paid work, such as fuel, vehicle maintenance, rental or financing, equipment, mobile data, and work-related fees. Their inclusion and classification depend on the study’s methodology. These expenses reduce the amount of income remaining from gross earnings.

Information contributed or recorded by workers about their own working activities and conditions, including earnings, expenses, time, trips, and platforms used. Contributions may come from manual records, location data shared with consent, or other worker-provided evidence. In Delivery Worker Atlas, these records support aggregated analyses intended to protect participants’ privacy.

cta.title: Is a term missing?
cta.description: If you did not find a term you consider important, or would like to suggest a new definition or a change to an existing term, please contact us. Your contribution helps keep the glossary more complete, accurate, and useful for everyone.

sourceNotes.editorialNote: Definitions are original summaries informed by the sources cited in each entry; DWA operational definitions should be checked against the final published methodology.
